newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin cold lingers, doctors say no heart danger.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin cold lingers, doctors say no heart danger.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin spent Wednesday at his country residence outside Moscow nursing a heavy cold but the surgeon who gave him a multiple heart bypass two months ago said there was no cause for alarm.
"He is staying at Gorky-9 and keeping to the same treatment, being partially confined to bed," a Kremlin spokesman said.
A spokeswoman later told Reuters that doctors would examine the 65-year-old president on Wednesday afternoon and release a medical bulletin later in the day (Eds: after 1400 GMT).

Renat Akchurin, the Russian surgeon who led the team that performed a quintuple bypass on Yeltsin's coronory arteries on November 5, told Itar-Tass news agency the cold was in no way related to the operation and posed no threat to his heart.
To suggest otherwise was "pure speculation", he said.

An official working for Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, said his office would probably announce later in the day whether the premier would leave as planned for a previously announced short holiday in the countryside near Moscow.

Chernomyrdin, 58, is Yeltsin's constitutional number two. He briefly took control of the state, including Russia's nuclear button, when Yeltsin was on the operating table. Less formally, Chernomyrdin seemed to be effectively running the country after Yeltsin fell ill shortly before being re-elected last July.
The president's absence fuelled a struggle for position among Kremlin officials that culminated in the October sacking of security adviser Alexander Lebed amid charges of coup plots.
Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov is supervising the medical team treating the president, who fell sick on Monday and was forced to cancel engagements for the next few days.
Akchurin said that although, in the two or three months after surgery, "it is better to avoid any illness, the president's cold can scarcely cause problems for the heart".
Yeltsin looked tired and pale during a meeting with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl near Moscow on Saturday.
His chief spokesman said on Monday the president had a "heavy cold" and a temperature of 37.5 degrees Celsius (99.5 Fahrenheit) but stressed it had nothing to do with his heart.
Russian media said several of the president's family, including his younger grandson Gleb and his wife Naina, had fallen victim to a cold epidemic sweeping Moscow over New Year.
Veteran Texan heart surgeon Michael DeBakey, who advised Akchurin during the heart surgery, told Reuters on Monday the president was recovering on schedule.

"Based on the reports I'm getting, it would appear his cardiac function has been virtually restored to normal," DeBakey said, adding that the surgery should even make him more resistant to infections like a cold.
He said he did not think the president's return to work at the end of last month had contributed to his catching cold.

Yeltsin is building a demanding schedule of meetings, including a summit of former Soviet states in Moscow on January 17, talks in the capital with French President Jacques Chirac on February 2 followed by a trip to the Netherlands and discussions with President Bill Clinton in the United States in March.
